title: "Australian Wine Sales Forecasting"
format: html
execute:
  warning: false
  message: false

Use this notebook to follow the analysis without opening the app. Change the example settings to try a different comparison. In the app, these settings come from the controls.

## 1. Load and prepare the sales data

Each row in the monthly time series represents one wine type and one month. Sales are measured in thousand liters.

```{r}
library(fpp3)
library(readr)
library(urca)

csv <- if (file.exists("data/AustralianWines.csv")) {
  "data/AustralianWines.csv"
} else {
  "../data/AustralianWines.csv"
}

wine <- read_csv(csv, na = "*", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  rename_with(trimws) |>
  rename(Sparkling = sparkling) |>
  mutate(Month = yearmonth(as.Date(paste0("01-", Month), "%d-%b-%y"))) |>
  pivot_longer(-Month, names_to = "Varietal", values_to = "Sales") |>
  as_tsibble(index = Month, key = Varietal)

selected_wines <- c("Fortified", "Red")
first_month <- yearmonth("1980 Jan")
last_month <- yearmonth("1994 Dec")

selected <- wine |>
  filter(Varietal %in% selected_wines) |>
  filter_index(as.character(first_month) ~ as.character(last_month))

autoplot(selected, Sales) +
  facet_wrap(vars(Varietal), scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Sales (thousand liters)")
```

## 2. Split the data

Models learn from the early months. The later months show how well those models predict new sales. Missing training values use the previous observed value for the same wine type.

```{r}
train_end <- yearmonth("1993 Dec")

training <- selected |>
  filter_index(. ~ as.character(train_end)) |>
  group_by(Varietal) |>
  fill(Sales, .direction = "down") |>
  ungroup()

validation <- selected |> filter_index(as.character(train_end + 1) ~ .)
```

## 3. Fit three models per wine type

TSLM uses a straight-line trend and a pattern for each month. ETS and ARIMA choose their settings using the training data.

```{r}
fits <- training |> model(
  TSLM = TSLM(Sales ~ trend() + season()),
  ETS = ETS(Sales),
  ARIMA = ARIMA(Sales)
)

# Show the chosen forms, including ETS components and ARIMA orders.
fits
```

## 4. Make forecasts

The first forecast has the length chosen for the chart. The second covers every validation month for scoring.

```{r}
h <- 12
chart_forecast <- forecast(fits, h = h)
validation_forecast <- forecast(fits, h = n_distinct(validation$Month))
```

## 5. Compare accuracy

Training scores show how well the models fit past sales. Validation scores show how well they predicted later months. Lower values are better.

```{r}
measures <- list(RMSE = RMSE, MAE = MAE, MAPE = MAPE)

training_scores <- fabletools::accuracy(fits, measures = measures)
validation_scores <- fabletools::accuracy(
  validation_forecast, selected, measures = measures
)

bind_rows(Training = training_scores, Validation = validation_scores, .id = "Period") |>
  select(Varietal, Period, Model = .model, RMSE, MAE, MAPE) |>
  arrange(Varietal, Period, RMSE) |>
  mutate(across(c(RMSE, MAE, MAPE), ~ round(.x, 2)))
```

## 6. Plot actual sales and forecasts

The gray line shows recent actual sales. Each model has its own panel so its 80% and 95% prediction bands stay easy to read.

```{r}
recent_sales <- selected |>
  filter(Month > train_end - 24, Month <= max(chart_forecast$Month))

autoplot(chart_forecast, recent_sales, level = c(80, 95)) +
  facet_grid(Varietal ~ .model, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Sales (thousand liters)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

## 7. About and reproduction

The data come from the AustralianWines.csv file supplied for ADS-506. To recreate the report figure in the app, select **Fortified** and **Red**, choose **January 1980 to December 1994**, set **December 1993** as the last training month, and choose **12 months** to predict. Leave all three models selected and show **24 months** of past sales. The app's **About** tab repeats these settings.
